summary: - Open with a direct 2‑sentence hook that addresses the viewer (“Your …”) and adds a vivid, unexpected comparison or fact; - Phrase the title as a concise question that references the viewer’s experience or a surprising outcome; - Keep the video under 30 seconds and avoid countdown timers unless the hook needs a timed reveal; - Use a single, eye‑catching emoji that matches the core subject in the title; - Highlight a counter‑intuitive detail in the first line to trigger curiosity instantly
winning_hooks: Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
The real T. rex probably couldn't run. Not even a jog.
One T. rex bite pressed down like three small cars stacked on its teeth.
avoid: Starting with vague statements like “Most X are …” without personal address
Using generic “Why” titles without implying a personal benefit or surprise
Long intros that exceed 5 seconds before the hook appears
next_experiment: Create two versions of a new Shorts: Version A uses a 2‑sentence hook that directly addresses the viewer and includes a vivid analogy (e.g., “Your smartphone battery dies faster than a cheetah sprint. Here’s why.”) with a question‑style title; Version B uses a generic hook and statement title. Run an A/B split test measuring stayed_pct to see which format boosts retention.
